events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip check for Phoenix after the Wednesday site change is mostly resolved.
events.interaction_goal: Turn the Phoenix plan into a concise departure checklist, confirm whether the shuttle plan is enough, and decide whether any seat or timing changes are worth making before travel.
events.scenario_brief: Two days before the Phoenix trip, the booked ATL-to-PHX nonstop flights and central hotel still fit the client agenda. The client confirms that a shuttle will take Maya from the hospital campus to the Scottsdale outpatient walkthrough on Wednesday, but the return timing is still approximate, so she wants a rideshare backup noted. Online check-in is opening, the weather looks clear in Phoenix but unsettled in Atlanta, and the hotel again confirms luggage storage, on-site dinner, and paid breakfast only. The remaining items are seat selection, Monday airport timing, early breakfast alternatives, Wednesday shuttle details, Thursday airport margin, and receipt capture.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new work-travel episode after the Phoenix client visit wraps.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Minneapolis trip, identify the viable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details Maya needs before sending an approval-ready plan.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from Phoenix, Maya is asked to plan a solo reporting workshop in Minneapolis for a Twin Cities healthcare client in early March. The likely travel pattern is Monday afternoon or evening arrival, Tuesday and Wednesday onsite sessions, and a Thursday return, but the client has not yet confirmed whether the workshop is at the downtown hospital building or a nearby administrative office. ATL-to-MSP nonstops are available, while cheaper one-stop itineraries add winter-connection risk. She wants a practical hotel with strong guest ratings, workable breakfast, and dinner access without needing a rental car. The unresolved details are the exact site, first required onsite time, Thursday closeout time, and whether the client expects her to use rideshares or local transit.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Minneapolis planning after the client confirms the downtown site and meeting schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main flight-and-hotel combinations and choose the package Maya should send to her manager for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the downtown Minneapolis hospital campus, a Tuesday 9:00 a.m. start, a full Wednesday workshop day, and a Thursday closeout expected to end around noon. The cleanest outbound is a Monday late-morning Delta nonstop that leaves time for hotel check-in and a short prep block, while the lower-cost one-stop option arrives later and adds a tight winter connection. Thursday return choices include a midafternoon nonstop that could be tight if the closeout runs long and an early-evening nonstop that gives more margin. Hotel options include a highly rated skyway-connected property with on-site dining and paid breakfast, a limited-service hotel with included breakfast but a longer rideshare to the campus, and a cheaper airport-area hotel that would complicate both mornings.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Minneapolis work trip from approval into booking before the fare hold expires.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Minneapolis flights and hotel, document the local-transport plan, and choose seats while the approved itinerary is still on hold.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the Monday late-morning nonstop, the early-evening Thursday return, and the skyway-connected downtown hotel as long as the hotel rate remains cancellable. The fare hold expires that night, and the hotel can add a high-floor quiet-room request away from elevators. Breakfast is not included, but there are early cafes in the connected complex, and the client says no rental car is needed. Seat maps show a few window seats toward the back on both flights, with most forward options limited to aisle or middle seats. The remaining items are booking confirmation, seat choice, no-car notes, hotel request wording, and receipt details for reimbursement.

events.continuity_hook: Final logistics pass for Minneapolis after booking and after the client sends badge and dinner details.
events.interaction_goal: Build a concise Minneapolis travel checklist and flag the few weather-sensitive decisions Maya should recheck the day before flying.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Minneapolis departure, the flights, downtown hotel, and no-car plan are booked, but a snow forecast could affect both ATL departures and MSP ground travel. The client sends badge instructions and asks Maya to be at the hospital security desk by 8:15 a.m. Tuesday. The hotel confirms luggage storage and on-site dinner service, but early check-in is not guaranteed and breakfast remains paid. A Wednesday team dinner has been moved to a restaurant several blocks from the hotel, so she wants to check whether walking through the skyway is realistic or if rideshare should be planned. The open items are airport timing, MSP transfer choice, Tuesday morning route, breakfast fallback, Wednesday dinner transportation, Thursday airport margin, and whether better window seats have opened.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new family leisure episode after the late-winter work trips.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the DC family trip, compare the airport and hotel-area tradeoffs, and identify what Maya needs to confirm with her spouse before narrowing options.
events.scenario_brief: After the Minneapolis workshop, Maya starts planning a family spring-break trip to Washington, DC with her spouse and child. The likely window is a four-night stay in early April, though they may shorten it to a long weekend if her spouse cannot take the full time off. Flights from Atlanta into DCA have the simplest ground logistics but are pricing higher, BWI has lower fares with a longer transfer, and IAD looks less convenient for the areas they want. Hotel choices are beginning to cluster around Penn Quarter, the Smithsonian area, and Capitol Hill, with tradeoffs between room size, included breakfast, casual dinner access, and walking distance to museums. The unresolved pieces are the exact dates, airport choice, nightly budget ceiling, and whether breakfast should outweigh a slightly larger room.
